result_text:
Tickets now carry an assigned support agent (a free-text name, nullable). It is stored on creation, returned by every ticket lookup and list you named, and kept when a ticket's status changes. All 10 ticket-related test classes pass offline, including a new test. Nothing is committed.

What changed:
- **`schema.sql`**: `support_ticket` has a new nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column.
- **`model/SupportTicket.java`**: the record gets an `agent` component. A 9-argument constructor is kept so existing callers still compile and get a null agent.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupportTicket` writes the agent, and all nine ticket `SELECT`s read it back.
- **`service/SupportTicketService.java`**: `changeStatus` carries the agent over. `create` gets an overload that takes an agent; the old signature delegates with null.
- **`SupportTicketTest.java`**: new `agentIsKeptInListsAndStatusChanges` test covering creation, lookup, a customer list, and closing.

Choices to review:
- The agent is a plain name string, since the codebase has no support-agent entity.
- There is no separate "assign agent" operation; the agent is set only when a ticket is created.
- `DemoScenario` still prints only ticket numbers, so the demo output doesn't show agents yet.
